prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Quick Desktop Controls Guide", "Learn how to summon, click, drag, and toggle your pet's desktop presence in a few simple taps.", "Desktop Shortcuts Overview"]
1: ["Select Your Pet Experience", "Pick a ready-to-play pet or craft a customized companion from your photos."]
2: ["Photo Clarity Inspection", "We checked your image to ensure the best rendering quality on your desktop."]
3: ["Summoning Your Desktop Pet", "Preparing desktop environment and initializing rendering engine..."]
4: ["Signing into an existing account safely recovers all previous pets and customizations."]
5: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Give your new companion a name. You can change this at any time in app settings."]
6: ["If pet initialization takes longer than 30 seconds, verify desktop notification permissions."]
7: ["Use the system tray icon anytime to quickly hide or show your desktop companion."]
8: ["Ready in 10s vs 2 mins custom"]
9: ["Sign In to Save Companion Data"]

verdicts.problem: Creates urgency or pressures choices using time comparisons
